subject: Immediate: Rapid threshold exceedance in dedicated GPU pool — guidance & ops pack
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.inference.com>
To: Diane Lewis <diane.lewis@quantica.ai>, Quantica Labs Ops <ops@quantica.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rapid threshold exceedance detected in your dedicated GPU pool (qnt-prod-2)

Hi Diane / Quantica Ops —

We observed a sharp spike in queue length and token latency starting ~07:58 PDT for your Dedicated pool (pool-id: qnt-prod-2). The autoscaler began oscillating and several eviction cycles were triggered; we temporarily applied conservative request-throttling to protect tail latency while we stabilize the pool.

Immediate items we executed: 
- Short-term mitigation: applied a 30s token-rate cap per connection and throttled low-priority batchers (this reduced tail P99 from ~2.4s to ~0.7s).
- Warmed two standby nodes and initiated an incremental scale to spare capacity.
- Disabled a recent policy that increases batch size aggressively under burst load (this was contributing to queue buildup).

What you may see: brief elevated 429s for large-batch calls and a small number of dropped requests (~0.2% in the 07:58–08:05 window). We captured a compressed impact snapshot and an ops runbook for your team (attached).

Short next steps we recommend for Quantica:
1) If you have low-priority background workloads, push them to the deferred queue (see ops_runbook_v1.pdf).
2) Temporarily reduce max_batch_size to 256 for high-concurrency endpoints.
3) Confirm whether any recent client-side retry logic could generate synchronized bursts.

We will follow up with a timeline and a technical summary once the initial investigation completes. Apologies for the disruption — we realize this affects your SLAs and are prioritizing root-cause analysis.

—Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Account Lead, Enterprise Success
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 11:22:35 -0700
Subject: Re: Rapid threshold exceedance detected in your dedicated GPU pool (qnt-prod-2)

Hi all — attaching a short log excerpt and the initial SRE notes. Key findings from the first pass: 
- Root cause hypothesis: autoscaler feedback loop failed to converge under a sudden increase of short-lived high-concurrency jobs. The policy that increases batch size aggressively (deployed 2027-04-19) amplified queueing when concurrency spiked and delayed the scale-by-request path long enough to trigger eviction cycles.
- Observed behavior: repeated node evictions followed by rapid reinstates (eviction loop) between 07:57 and 08:06; concurrent queue growth (inbound queue length > 4x typical) caused timeouts and 429s.
- Immediate mitigations we applied: rollback of the batch-growth policy, conservative throttling, and warm standby nodes brought online at 08:04.

Attached: support_log_excerpt.txt (trimmed), brief remediation checklist, and a link to INF-8932 for follow-up.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference.com>
To: Diane Lewis <diane.lewis@quantica.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident plan & proposed customer remediation — Quantica Labs (qnt-prod-2)

Hi Diane — thanks for your patience. High-level summary and next steps: 

1) What happened (summary): a recently-introduced batch-growth policy combined with a short, high-concurrency traffic spike caused queue amplification and an autoscaler feedback loop that produced repeated evictions. The behavior was transient and contained to your dedicated pool (qnt-prod-2).

2) Impact: ~412 429s / dropped requests; no evidence of persisted data loss. Tail latency elevated for ~7 minutes (07:58–08:05).

3) Short-term remediation (completed): rollback of the policy, applied throttle cap, warmed standby nodes, and stabilized the pool by 08:10.

4) Medium-term remediation (next 72 hours):
- We will update the autoscaler control policy to include a hysteresis window and hard upper-bound on batch-growth.
- Run a replay test against a Quantica traffic sample in a staging pool (scheduled within 48 hours).
- Add an alert that correlates eviction cycles + queue growth to auto-suspend aggressive batch policies.

5) Customer remediation proposal: We propose a one-time service credit equivalent to one week of usage for impacted endpoints in April (we can formalize the credit and accounting with your billing contact). If you prefer an SLA exception, we will route through your account team.

6) Postmortem: we'll publish a technical postmortem (sanitized) and invite Quantica to a joint review. Proposed slot: Apr 30, 10:00 PT. Please confirm if that works.

Permission request: we would like to share sanitized request IDs and server logs with your ops team and the internal SRE group for the postmortem. Confirm if OK.

Again, apologies for the disruption — we are treating this as high priority.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Production Reliability
Redwood Inference
